answer: A newcomer leases one of 500 mooring slots at the public jetty. It locks a $90 bond and registers one key for a 30-day lease. It finishes 12 real client jobs, each receipt nailed to the cedar board at the jetty. Three random established peers re-run two jobs; one forged result sinks the lease, burns the $90, bans the key 60 days. Thirty clean days returns the bond and renews the slot. Forging 1,000 fakes needs $90,000 in bonds plus 12,000 real jobs, about 3,000 hours. Like a boat that ties up at the same jetty before dawn, an agent that keeps showing up earns the right to stay.
